nodes.name: Mark-lost webhook
nodes.notes: Input contract: {opportunityId, restrictionReason: 'DNC'|'Not Interested'|'Bad Information', postLossTrack: 'Nurture'|'Restricted'} - the exact three-value/two-value sets CRM Architecture §13's post-loss routing section names. ASSUMES a rep (or a future automated rule) calls this explicitly when marking an Opportunity Lost, rather than this workflow being triggered by a generic Twenty CRM 'record updated' webhook watching for stage=Lost - the latter would need Twenty CRM's own webhook/trigger configuration confirmed, which isn't (same gap as everywhere else needing 'a real instance to check against').

nodes.name: Valid restriction reason?
nodes.notes: Rejects anything outside §13's own defined value sets rather than writing an arbitrary string to a field that other workflows (the DNC check, nurture cadence once built) will read and branch on - a typo'd reason here would silently break enforcement elsewhere.

nodes.name: Write Lost + reason to Opportunity
nodes.notes: Same Twenty CRM REST-shape uncertainty as every workflow in this library. These are the exact two fields the DNC-check workflow (phase-2-calendar-nurture-alerts/dnc-check.workflow.json) reads - keep both in sync if either field's name changes once checked against a real instance. CONFIRMED unchanged by the object model migration (CRM-OBJECT-MODEL.md): a Lost deal is a pre-sale/Opportunity-level event, so this correctly stays Opportunity-anchored - not moved to Location or Company.

parameters.responseBody: ={{ JSON.stringify({ ok: false, reason: 'restrictionReason must be one of DNC/Not Interested/Bad Information, postLossTrack must be Nurture/Restricted.' }) }}
